title: Irish Potatoes Grown in Certain Designated Counties in Idaho, and Malheur County, Oregon; Increased Assessment Rate
summary:
The U.S. Department of Agriculture has finalized a small fee increase to fund the local potato program for parts of Idaho and Malheur County, Oregon. The assessment on potatoes handled in the region goes from $0.002 to $0.003 per 100 pounds for the 2024–2025 season and beyond, effective October 22, 2025.

This change is meant to keep the program’s budget in balance and rebuild modest reserves after several years of drawing them down. The Idaho–Eastern Oregon Potato Committee expects about 34 million 100-pound units to ship this season, which at the new rate would bring in about $102,000. That covers the approved budget of roughly $99,500 for basic operations like administration, audits and compliance, banking and insurance, IT support, and limited committee travel, and adds a small amount back to reserves. The reserve target is about one year of expenses. There are no new reporting or paperwork requirements.

Who benefits? The regional industry gets a steady, locally run program with predictable funding to handle its routine oversight and compliance work. That can support stability and planning for producers and handlers, most of whom are small businesses. The fee remains tiny compared to crop value; based on recent prices, it works out to about three-tenths of a cent per 100 pounds, or roughly 0.024 percent of producer revenue.

Who might be negatively affected? Handlers will pay a little more, and some of that cost could be passed back to growers. While the increase is just one-tenth of a cent per 100 pounds, any added cost can matter when margins are tight. People concerned about fees that continue indefinitely may also take note, though the committee reviews the budget and rate each year in public meetings.

This decision followed the usual public process. A proposal was published last fall, stakeholders had a chance to weigh in, and the final rule reflects the committee’s unanimous recommendation to align funding with current needs.
